scope: First reasoned review of three supplied samples; static analysis, offline decoding, no live payload execution

samples.marker_line: BrightData infected updater: concealed native stage; add decoder
execution_evidence: Original PE entry 0x1401d465c calls 0x1400010c3. That routine jumps among overwritten host-code gaps, saves registers/stack and calls VirtualAlloc(0,0xffb46,0x3000,4).

It reads RVA 0xc9e200 and reconstructs 0xbe006 bytes in 14-byte groups using word-add, dword-subtract, byte-add, byte-add, word-add and dword-add operations. The keys are immediate operands, not names or reputation.

At 0x140016e08 it rewinds the output cursor; it passes this buffer to VirtualProtect with PAGE_EXECUTE_READ, then invokes buffer+0xbd4b8. The new rule binds the contiguous buffer-base/protection-shaped call/offset invocation and requires the scattered decoder plus VirtualProtect.

The recovered native loader walks PEB/export tables, allocates memory, applies an incrementing XOR pass and repeating 32-byte header-key XOR, then invokes RtlDecompressBuffer with 0x102. Offline emulation was confined to the decoder and a hooked allocation stub; the sample was not run.

LZNT1 output is 514560 bytes with PNG magic, a relocated PE-header pointer and scrambled import names. Its custom mapper explicitly accepts PNG magic and maps this disguised image. An analyst-only reconstructed PE restored MZ/e_lfanew/PE signatures for tooling; it is not the original binary.

The mapped DLL export a is invoked. It contains OOXML CustomXML/native-thread VBA templates and code references to [Content_Types].xml, customXml/customXml1.xml and word/vbaProject.bin in the same package-editing routine (0x18001bdef onward). Existing ooxml-native-thread-infection-templates fires on this recovered stage.

Embedded BrightData components carry Bright Data Ltd signatures and consistent build/version data. Their real VMDetector.IsVM and DetectVM methods compare WMI machine/GPU data and virtual-adapter values. The three VM-display findings are accurate dual-use detections and remain suspicious.

The original host CreateFiber/SwitchToFiber call sites at 0x1400d10ef/0x1400d1171 belong to OpenSSL crypto/async/async.c (source path at 0x140226330), not the injected decoder. Nt-section names and the WinHTTP/process/registry APIs are independently present. The former rules did not bind these APIs into the execution/staging relationships their descriptions claimed.
samples.deployment_limits: Installation circumstances and authorization are unavailable; verdict rests on the bytes and packaging, not on an assumed victim context.
samples.coverage_limit: One hostile outer-file detection is supported. The decoded DLL exposes OOXML/macro infection and further masking, but those bytes remain behind a custom arithmetic/XOR/LZNT1 loader that atomscan does not unpack. The stage was decoded and scanned separately; no cleartext stage trait was falsely made an outer-file claim. Adding more hostile variants of the same decoder-to-call chain would duplicate one behavior.
samples.classifier_disagreement: Local model still reports alert level -1/confidence 0 despite the independently verified infection. New hostile rule fires. This is a classifier/automatic-unpacking coverage gap; inaccurate API claims were not restored to inflate its score.

samples.identity: PowerShell TCP command dispatcher in a batch launcher
samples.marker_line: PowerShell TCP dispatcher: hidden remote eval and output return
execution_evidence: Batch suppresses echo and launches powershell -nop -w hidden -c with inline source.
Creates Net.Sockets.TCPClient(10.0.0.13,4444), obtains its NetworkStream, allocates a byte buffer and loops on stream.Read.

Decodes received bytes with ASCIIEncoding.GetString, evaluates the decoded variable with iex, captures stdout/stderr through Out-String, ASCII-encodes the result and writes/flushes it to the same TCP stream.

The explicit comment and private destination are consistent with a demonstration fixture. They do not remove the standalone hidden, unauthenticated remote-command execution surface; a security engineer finding it deployed would treat it as likely malicious absent lab/operator authorization.
samples.deployment_limits: Installation circumstances and authorization are unavailable; verdict rests on the bytes and packaging, not on an assumed victim context.
samples.coverage_limit: Two independent hostile claims are supported: remote command evaluation and concealment of that command channel. TCP read/write, output return, ASCII decoding and interpreter flags remain notable. A third independent hostile behavior was not found; no persistence, credential theft or separate payload staging was invented.
samples.classifier_disagreement: Local alert level improves from -1/confidence 0 to 25/confidence 92 after the independently supported concealment detection.

samples.identity: Obfuscated Ethereum recipient-derived Node stage loader
samples.marker_line: Ethereum stage loader: XOR HTTP eval and hidden Node children
execution_evidence: Recovered the string-array rotation (160 rotations, decoder offset 0x92) with a bounded offline parser. No network requests, eval or child spawning were executed during decoding.

Module load immediately invokes run(). It queries Ethereum JSON-RPC endpoints, locates transactions from the configured sender using candidate blocks/nonce searches and falls back to a Blockscout account indexer.
decodeAddress consumes the selected tx.to recipient, hex-decodes it and formats selected byte slices as two IPv4 addresses. These addresses supply stage endpoints and child global configuration.

Requests two HTTP stages at /0x/cls and /0x/ls over port 443. A GET body is repeating-key XOR-decoded to UTF-8; an empty-body/header path or HEAD fallback reads x-payload-b64, Base64-decodes and applies the same XOR decoder.

The /0x/cls stage is indirectly evaled in the current process and launched in a detached hidden node -e child. The /0x/ls stage is launched in a detached hidden Node child only. Children ignore stdio and are unrefed. Catches discard errors.

Five existing hostile detections accurately cover recipient-based rendezvous, XOR/HTTP inline staging, header/blockchain inline staging, child evaluation and hidden-child evasion. The child-evaluation observation was relocated to the payload sink with exact consumers preserved. No final downloaded payload or stolen data was established.
samples.deployment_limits: Installation circumstances and authorization are unavailable; verdict rests on the bytes and packaging, not on an assumed victim context.
samples.coverage_limit: Five supported hostile detections retained; no additional distinct behavior gap identified in the available first-stage source.
samples.classifier_disagreement: Local alert level remains 25/confidence 92; no remaining disagreement at this reported gate.

classifier_limitation: The installed scanner warns that model feature schema v18 predates expected v21. Reported local alert levels are recorded without treating raw probability as ground truth.

corrections.why: API references establish a profile, not ordering, stage mapping or fiber callback provenance; actual host fiber code is OpenSSL async scheduling.

No required obfuscation or download-to-activation link. Names, file APIs, registry APIs and large string count do not establish a dropper. Updater-name reference retained separately under fs/path/basename.
Only a bounded GetString/eval assignment syntax relationship; no transport or variable binding. Remote-command composite continues to require TCP/read/eval evidence.

Required acquisition-to-evaluation chain belongs to its payload sink. Exact references and relevant JS parent selectors were updated. PHP-only and Python-only selectors cannot consume this JS/TS rule.

regression.result: All original hostile findings retained. The two PowerShell fixtures only lose the misclassified suspicious syntax trait, whose identical predicate is retained as notable. Signed BrightData embedded-member detections remain unchanged.

new_controls.api-profile-only.exe: old hostile fiber rule fired; corrected neutral profile retained, no hostile claim

regression.basis_for_shared_correction: Actual host OpenSSL fiber scheduling was traced; synthetic near misses are additional controls, not the sole basis for weakening a technique.
